chunks: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

"Whenever the water overcomes the smell of the carcass, then perform wudu (ablution) from the water and drink. But when the water changes, or the taste changes, then do not perform wudu (ablution) from it and do not drink."

These two reports indicate that when water changes in its color or its taste, then it is not permissible to drink it or to purify oneself with it, whether it is still or flowing, because the wording is unrestricted and not qualified. And there has already preceded, in what came before, that which also serves as an indication of what we have mentioned; and mentioning it there is sufficient and makes repeating it unnecessary, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills. As for the report which he narrated:

key_terms.تَغَيَّرَ: underwent alteration in a legally significant way
key_terms.رِيحِ ٱلْجِيفَةِ: the odor of a carcass affecting the water
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءُ: water used for drinking and ritual purification

ai.seo_question: When does changed water become impermissible for wudu (ablution) and drinking in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage states a legal ruling regarding water affected by a carcass: if the water remains dominant over the odor, it may be used for wudu (ablution) and drinking, but if the water itself or its taste changes, it may not be used. The accompanying authorial note generalizes the ruling to changed water, whether still or flowing, as unsuitable for both drinking and ritual purification.
